passages.title: Passage I (Questions 21–25)
passages.body:
Conventional education makes independent thinking extremely difficult. Conformity leads to mediocrity. To be different from the group or to resist environment is not easy and is often risky as long as we worship success. The urge to be successful, which is the pursuit of reward whether in the materials or in the so-called spiritual sphere, the search for inward or outward security, the desire for comfort—this whole process smothers discontent, put an end to spontaneity and breed fear; and fear blocks the intelligent understanding of life. With increasing age, dullness of mind and heart sets in.

In seeking comfort, we generally find a quiet corner in life where there is a minimum of conflict, and then we are afraid to step out of that seclusion. This fear of life, this fear of struggle and of a new experience, kills in us the spirit of adventure; our whole upbringing and education have made us afraid to be different from our neighbour, afraid to think contrary to the established pattern of society, falsely respectful of authority and tradition.

Fortunately, there are a few who are in earnest, who are willing to examine our human problems without the prejudice of the right or of the left; but in the vast majority of us, there is no real spirit of discontent, or revolt. When we yield uncomprehendingly to environment, any spirit of revolt that may have had died down, and our responsibilities soon put an end to it.
passages.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

passages.title: Passage II (Questions 26–30)
passages.body:
Noise is a common problem in both urban and rural areas, traffic noise in particular. Trees and shrubs are not only visually attractive but also can make effective noise barriers. Therefore when space permits we have to plant more trees and shrubs in areas where there is noise problem. By doing this noise can be reduced by six decibels over a distance of 30 metres.

The only thing we have to keep in mind is that the planting should be particularly dense; the trees which have dense foliage and relatively vertical orientation of arrangements should be planted. It will completely screen the source of noise. If there is any gap in barrier it will still allow noise to penetrate. Single layer of trees is worthless as a noise barrier. Due to inter-reflection, multi-rows of trees are more effective. The planted trees must be taller. We can reduce noise level by 1·5 decibels with each additional 3 feet of tree height.

When the opportunity to use trees is restricted a combination of shrubs and tall grass can be used. Instead of tarmac or gravel surfaces soft grass ground cover is preferable. It will absorb noise rather than reflect it. Rows of trees, shrubs, crotons, ground covering plants, climbers and their flowers not only reduce noise and provide a beautiful backyard they also help block wind, provide shade, and absorb traffic pollution.
passages.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

passages.title: Cloze passage (Questions 71–80)
passages.body: It sounds like (71) _____ great idea. People get instantly excited when they hear (72) _____ phrase ‘education for peace’ or the title of a course that calls itself ‘peace Education’. About a decade ago, I proposed such (73) _____ course in my institute. The idea of a course (74) _____ ‘peace education’ had occurred to me on the way back from one of the neighbouring countries where I met students of class IX. I could not find (75) _____ difference (76) _____ Indian students and their counterparts in the other country on peace (77) _____ living together. It made me think that if one learns to live with a conflict, life grows across it like grass (78) _____ trees. The arguments and stances children took demonstrated (79) _____ peace comes from understanding a conflict well, not necessarily (80) _____ solving it.
passages.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.theme: Past perfect continuous with a past period
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__He had been doing__ (a) __the job of a physician__ (b) __during the 1990s.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'He had been doing the job of a physician during the 1990s' is correct: the verb form, the noun phrase and the time phrase all agree.
Step 2: There is no error.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__He said__ (a) __that he preferred__ (b) __coffee than tea.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'Prefer' takes 'to', not 'than'.
Step 2: Correct form: 'preferred coffee to tea'. Part (c) is wrong.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.question:

__All that__ (a) __glitters__ (b) __are not gold.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'All that glitters' is treated as singular, so the verb must be 'is not gold'.
Step 2: 'are' in part (c) is wrong.
Answer: (c).

questions.question:

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Our greatest glory__ (a) __is not in never falling__ (b) __but in rising every time we fell.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: The sentence states a general truth in the present tense ('is not in never falling').
Step 2: The last part should also be present: 'every time we fall'. 'Fell' in part (c) is wrong.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Man has progressed with science and technology.
S6: What was difficult and impossible is now easy and possible.
P: He is on the road to conquer other planets.
Q: Now with scientific knowledge and technical know-how he has done what was impossible.
R: Hitherto he had been backward.
S: He has reached the moon.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: After S1, R gives the earlier backward state ('Hitherto').
Step 2: Q says what he can do 'now', S gives the moon example, and P ends with the next goal before S6.
Answer: (c) RQSP.
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: We drink more water during summers.
S6: There are variations in weather conditions during different seasons.
P: On the other hand in north-eastern states, winters are mild except in the hills.
Q: Because in North India, both the seasons have extreme weather conditions.
R: School clothes during the summer is different from the winter.
S: Why do you wear lighter clothes during summers and heavy woollen clothes during the winter in north India?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: R links clothes to the seasons, and S asks why north India needs light and heavy clothes.
Step 2: Q answers with 'Because ... extreme weather', then P contrasts the north-eastern states, leading to S6.
Answer: (b) RSQP.
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Policy, like many other terms, is a complex concept.
S6: Public policy is the outcome of the struggle between government and powerful groups.
P: It is form of government control usually expressed in a law, a legislation, a regulation or an order.
Q: Public policy is what a government chooses as guidance for action.
R: A policy may be general or specific, broad or narrow, simple or complex, public or private, written or unwritten.
S: It takes different forms.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: 'It takes different forms' (S) follows the complex concept in S1, and R lists those forms.
Step 2: Q moves to public policy as a choice, P says it is government control, and S6 ends with the outcome of struggle.
Answer: (a) SRQP.
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: The dhoti kurta is a traditional lungi-type garment worn by men in India.
S6: Gandhi ji usually wore a simple shawl with his dhoti.
P: It is commonly worn with a loose long tunic.
Q: This he started wearing after he abandoned his western attire of pants and shirt.
R: A dhoti, made of homespun khadi cotton cloth, was the garment favoured by Gandhi ji.
S: The dhoti is rectangular piece of unstitched cloth, around five yards long, wrapped around the midriff and tucked between the legs.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: S describes the dhoti and P ('It is commonly worn ...') follows.
Step 2: R brings in Gandhi ji, Q ('This he started wearing ...') follows R, and S6 says what he wore with it.
Answer: (c) SPRQ.
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Languages in contact with each other cause change.
S6: Changes often occur first in informal and casual language.
P: The increasing use of English in many parts of the world affect both local languages and English.
Q: Language contact has long been recognised as a major engine of change.
R: This gives rise to new, hybrid language varieties.
S: A historical example is that of Danish and English which led to a major shift in the vocabulary and grammar of English.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: Q restates S1 as a long-recognised idea, and S gives a historical example.
Step 2: P moves to today's English, and R ('This gives rise to new, hybrid language varieties') follows P.
Answer: (b) QSPR.
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Urbanisation in India has become an important and irreversible process.
S6: As per the Census of India 2011, the urban population is increasing rapidly.
P: The 2030 development agenda of the United Nations has emphasised the role of sustainable cities for making cities inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable.
Q: This shows that India is in the midst of transition from a predominantly rural to a quasi-urban society.
R: The process of urbanisation has been characterized by a dramatic increase in the number of large cities.
S: It is an important determinant of national economic growth and poverty reduction.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: S ('It is an important determinant ...') follows S1 and R describes the process.
Step 2: Q ('This shows ...') draws a conclusion from R and P adds the UN agenda. S6 then ends with the Census figures.
Answer: (c) SRQP.
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Ethics is a branch of philosophy concerned with the distinction between right and wrong (morals) and the ultimate worth of actions or things (values).
S6: But values can be either inherent or conferred.
P: For many philosophers, only humans are moral agents, being capable of acting morally or immorally.
Q: Environmental ethics asks about the moral relationships between humans and the world around us.
R: Ethics evaluated the relationship, rules, principles or codes that require or forbid certain conduct.
S: Value is a measure of the worth of something.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: R continues the definition of ethics (rules and codes).
Step 2: Q narrows to environmental ethics, P says only humans are moral agents, and S defines value, leading to S6 'But values can be either inherent or conferred'.
Answer: (a) RQPS.
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: The Constitution of India, introduced on 26 January 1950, laid down certain basic principles and values.
S6: The Constitution guaranteed all citizens equality before the law and equality of opportunity in government employment.
P: It was also to be a federation with demarcation of spheres of action between the Union Government and the State Governments.
Q: India was to be a secular and democratic republic with a parliamentary system based on adult franchise.
R: These include: freedom of speech and expression, freedom to assemble peacefully etc.
S: It guaranteed all Indian citizens certain fundamental rights.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: Q gives the republic, and P adds ('also') the federation.
Step 2: S says it guaranteed fundamental rights, and R ('These include ...') lists them. S6 then covers equality.
Answer: (a) QPSR.
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: The National Health Policy 2017 envisages creation of a digital health technology eco-system.
S6: Secondly, offering financial protection up to ₹5 lakhs per year per family for the deprived 10 crores plus households.
P: Ayushman Bharat comprising twin missions is set to transform the nation’s health system.
Q: This will also foster a linkage across public and private healthcare.
R: The policy aims at developing an integrated health information system that serves the need of all stakeholder and improves efficiency, transparency.
S: This will be carried out by operationalising firstly 1.5 lakh health and wellness centres offering preventive and primary care.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: R follows S1 with what the policy aims to do, and Q ('This will also foster ...') extends it.
Step 2: P introduces Ayushman Bharat and its twin missions, and S says 'firstly' how it will be carried out. S6 begins 'Secondly'.
Answer: (c) RQPS.
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Ecology, history and geography determine the distribution of organisms.
S6: Others prefer to interpret biogeographical history through vicariance (range-splitting) events.
P: Some historical biogeographers are interested in finding centre-of-origins.
Q: Most species distributions result from a combination of all these factors.
R: But biogeographers tend to specialise in ecological aspects (ecological biogeography) or historical aspects.
S: Ecological biogeographers are interested in the effects of environmental factors.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: Q sums up S1 ('all these factors'), and R says biogeographers specialise ('But').
Step 2: S describes the ecological group and P the historical group, which leads to S6 'Others prefer ...'.
Answer: (a) QRSP.
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

He said that he ______ when he lost all his investment in the stock market.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Was broken' is the official answer in the key, which reads it as 'was left broken' (ruined).
Step 2: (b) 'was broke' is the informal 'out of money'. (c) and (d) are ungrammatical.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

The man in black thought that he was ______ selected for the team to play at the national level.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'One of the' must be followed by a plural noun.
Step 2: 'one of the players selected' fits.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

When she ______ her friend after a period of two decades her throat choked.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Her throat choked' is past, so the first clause takes the simple past: 'met'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

The portrait of the lady conveys ______ it appears.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'More than it appears' is the natural comparison: the portrait suggests more than what is visible.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

A biography is ______ person’s life history.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: A biography is about a person's life history; 'person's' needs the article 'a'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

She told me that she ______ her degree by 2023.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'She told me' is a past reporting verb, so 'will have completed' shifts to 'would have completed'.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

What is the name of the person ______ daughter married your cousin last year?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: Possession is shown with 'whose': the person's daughter.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

The world is changing ______ that the rich become richer and the poor become poorer.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'In such a way that' joins the manner to its result.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

Had I been informed beforehand, I ______ it to the celebrations.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Had I been informed' is the past unreal condition, so 'could have made' follows.
Step 2: (c) 'would have' lacks a main verb.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

Indian perspective of life informs that leading a life of greed ______ in unhappiness.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Result in' takes 'in', and the general truth is in the future tense.
Step 2: (a) 'lead' would need 'to', (b) and (d) are ungrammatical.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

His arguments are not valid. People consider it __bombastic__
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Bombastic' means high-sounding and wordy. Its opposite is plain and 'straight forward'.
Step 2: 'Verbose' is a synonym.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

The decision was __absurd__ for many of the members of the team
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Absurd' means unreasonable. The opposite is 'reasonable'.
Step 2: 'Bizarre' and 'meaningless' are close to absurd.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

Relatives of __deceased__ have been informed about the accident
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Deceased' means dead. The opposite is 'alive'.
Step 2: 'Dead' is a synonym; 'survived' is a verb form.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

At last she was able to get some __solace__ as the matter has been resolved amicably
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Solace' is comfort in distress. The opposite is 'aggravation' (making things worse).
Step 2: 'Comfort' and 'relief' are synonyms; 'punishment' is not an opposite.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

Twenty first century has turned out to be a century of problems __contrary__ to the thinking that it would be a better time
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Contrary to' means opposite to. The opposite is 'similar'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

The poet said that poetry is a __spontaneous__ overflow of powerful feelings
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Spontaneous' means unplanned and natural. The opposite is 'deliberate'.
Step 2: 'Prepared' fits less well, since 'deliberate' means done on purpose.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

Language is an instrument for __asserting__ one’s identity, attitude and perspective
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Asserting' means stating firmly. The opposite is 'denying'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

He has been __exonerated__ as he tendered an apology
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Exonerated' means cleared of blame. The opposite is 'convicted' (found guilty).
Step 2: 'Pardoned' is a synonym.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

__Persuasion__ is essential for people to work as a team
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Persuasion' means convincing someone to do something. The opposite is 'discouraging'.
Step 2: 'Convincing' is a synonym.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

Every habitat has some __distinctive__ vegetation which defines the eco-system
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Distinctive' means characteristic and different. The opposite is 'common'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

Having got excited she opened up the Pandora’s Box which led to lot of __commotion__
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Commotion' is noisy confusion. 'Uproar' is the nearest.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

The __inherent__ danger in the problem is that it would lead to many more problems
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Inherent' means existing as a natural part of something, so 'inbuilt'.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

The officer was __reprimanded__ by the court for delaying the case
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Reprimanded' means formally scolded. 'Admonished' is the nearest.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

Some people think that their strength is __perpetual__
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Perpetual' means never ending, so 'ever lasting'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

One’s actions __exemplify__ one’s attitude and values
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Exemplify' means to show by example, so 'demonstrate'.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

The __crux__ of the issue was that there was no evidence to prove the accused guilty of the act
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Crux' is the decisive or central point, so 'core'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

Each child develops his/her __competency__ based on the contexts and the inputs for learning
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Competency' means ability or skill, so 'capability'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

He appears to be very __haughty__, but he is a humble person
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Haughty' means arrogantly proud. 'Arrogant' is the nearest.
Step 2: 'Modest' is the opposite, as the sentence itself suggests with 'but ... humble'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

The newly appointed secretary is __industrious__
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Industrious' means hard-working, so 'diligent'.
Step 2: 'Indolent' is the opposite.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

The __indignant__ attitude of the speaker made the groups unhappy
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Indignant' means angry at unfair treatment, so 'resentful'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

The preacher said, “No one is __above__ the all powerful”
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Above' comes before the noun phrase 'the all powerful' and shows its relation to 'no one', so it is a preposition.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

The __most beautiful__ seven monkeys of the landlord were taken for a stroll
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Most beautiful' describes the monkeys, so it works as an adjective (a superlative adjective phrase).
Step 2: The key treats it as an adjective.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

__Alas!__ He has been defeated
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Alas!' is an exclamation of sorrow, so it is an interjection.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

The man __who__ is in the green shift is the chief of the day
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Who' introduces the clause 'who is in the green shift' and refers back to 'the man', so it is a relative pronoun.
Step 2: UPSC's key marks (b) 'Relative noun', the option that names the relative function. (a) 'Pronoun' is also true in a broad sense, so treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

He has been living in the jungle for long __and__ he knows all the animals here
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'And' joins two equal clauses, so it is a coordinating conjunction.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

They have been driving __since__ early morning
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Since' comes before the time phrase 'early morning' and links it to the verb, so it is a preposition.
Answer: (d).

Note: This question has been lightly edited from the printed paper for clarity and a single defensible answer.
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

__This__ time we woke up to the virus related diseases
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'This' points to 'time', so it is a demonstrative (a demonstrative adjective).
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

Love your neighbour as __thyself__
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Thyself' is the old reflexive form of 'yourself', so it is a pronoun.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

Ravi __won__ the match with a huge margin
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Won' takes the object 'the match', so it is a transitive verb.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

There was an __exultation__ in the group
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'An exultation' follows the article 'an' and names a feeling of joy, so it is a noun.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

Sheela has been at the receiving end ______
questions.opt_c: she had been proud of it
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'At the receiving end' means suffering ill treatment, and 'but she is very honest' gives the natural contrast.
Step 2: (c) and (d) lack a connector.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

Elam has no other option ______
questions.opt_d: he has to accept the challenge
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'No option but to accept' is the fixed pattern.
Step 2: (d) is a run-on sentence without a conjunction.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

Although the group has been acquitted ______
questions.opt_a: they are under the watch of police
questions.opt_b: they are free to do anything
questions.opt_c: there is no suspicion in them
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'Although' needs a contrast with 'acquitted'. 'They are under the watch of police' contrasts with the freedom an acquittal suggests.
Step 2: The other options agree with acquittal instead of contrasting it.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

Unless you fulfil the essential qualifications ______
questions.opt_a: you will be called for the interview
questions.opt_b: you shall be selected for the post
questions.opt_c: you will not be called for the interview
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'Unless' means 'if not', so the result must be negative: 'you will not be called'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

The company’s bid for the contract is rejected ______
questions.opt_a: since it filled all the conditions
questions.opt_b: for the company fulfilled the conditions
questions.opt_c: for the company had not been in the goodwill list
questions.opt_d: since the deposit in the account is found less than required
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: A bid is rejected when a condition is not met, so (d) gives a valid reason.
Step 2: (a) and (b) say the conditions were met, which would not cause rejection.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

I could not sleep ______
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'Could not sleep despite being very tired' is a logical contrast.
Step 2: (a) and (d) give tiredness as a cause of sleeplessness, which is illogical. (c) 'in spite of being sleepless' is circular.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

She married him ______
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'Because of' takes a noun phrase ('his nature').
Step 2: 'Because' needs a clause, 'since' needs a clause, and 'in spite' needs 'of'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

I will come to meet you ______
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'In case you want' says I will come if you want me to.
Step 2: (c) and (d) do not fit the sense.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

If you had planned the work well ______
questions.opt_a: you shall have completed it on time
questions.opt_b: you could complete it on time
questions.opt_c: you will complete it on time
questions.opt_d: you could have completed it on time
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'If you had planned' is the past unreal condition, so the result is 'could have completed'.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

You can use my computer ______
questions.opt_a: as long as you can’t use any external drive
questions.opt_b: as long as you used any external drive
questions.opt_c: as long as you do not use any external drive
questions.opt_d: as long as you shall use any external drive
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'As long as' sets a condition in the present tense: 'as long as you do not use any external drive'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

Don’t go ______ the wind, you will face the music later.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Go with the wind' means to follow the easy popular course.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

He has been considered ______ honest contestant in the competition.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound (the 'h' is silent), so 'an'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

Don’t read ______ the lines. Read the lines.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Read between the lines' means to look for hidden meaning.
Step 2: The printed item is awkward: it repeats 'the lines' with no contrast, but the fixed phrase still points to 'between'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

The village possesses ______ scenic beauty.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: The key accepts 'a' here, reading 'a scenic beauty' as a singular. 'Some' is also grammatical with an uncountable noun, so treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

He is all out to blame everyone ______ his mistakes.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Blame someone for' is the correct pattern.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

This is ______ unique system of governance where everyone is the government.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Unique' begins with a 'y' sound, so it takes 'a'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

I will take care ______ myself. You don’t bother about me.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Take care of' is the fixed phrase.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

She is considered ______ nightingale of the college for her melodious voice.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: A unique title such as 'the nightingale of the college' takes the definite article.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

The room is a bit dark. Could you please turn ______ the light?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: A dark room needs the light 'turned on'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2021 English set A (set code XVWS-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

Don’t walk so fast! I can’t keep ______ with you.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Keep up with' means to stay at the same pace.
Answer: (c).
